items.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995
items.q: Yeah, well, Basie was playing the piano in that band of course. And sometime down the line, Benny died.

ctx.x: We are filming some interviews with some of the United States of America’s greatest jazz artists for Hamilton College. We are very privileged to have two members of the Count Basie Orchestra with us today. We have Frank Foster and Bill Hughes. My name is Mike Woods and I am a professor at Hamilton College, and my colleague, Monk Rowe, teaches saxophone also at the college. I’d like to start and ask you guys some questions about the Basie band and how it got started. Tell us how the Basie band kind of evolved out…

Yeah, well, Basie was playing the piano in that band of course. And sometime down the line, Benny died. And the guys decided they wanted to get something going, and they formed a group, I think it was a small group at that point, but they decided that they wanted Basie to do the out front thing. And that’s really how he came to be the band leader. I don’t think he planned that at all, but it happened that all the guys liked him, you know, so they chose him to be the front man. That’s pretty generally how he got…
Thought he was easy going, so he became a leader?
